front: What is the retrieval unit in Vision RAG, and how is it obtained?
back: A whole rendered PDF page image, embedded and retrieved directly as pixels -- no text extraction or OCR happens anywhere in the pipeline.

front: How does Vision RAG differ from Multimodal RAG, per the page's own note?
back: Multimodal RAG still extracts and chunks text (plus pulls out figures); Vision RAG never extracts text at all -- a whole page is the retrieval unit and is what the LLM reads at generation time.

front: What scoring mechanism does Vision RAG use instead of a single pooled vector per page?
back: Late interaction (MaxSim): for each query token, take its single highest dot product against any page patch, then sum those per-token maxima into the page's score.

front: Why can't a mean-pooled single vector per page replace MaxSim without losing anything?
back: Pooling averages a strong local match (e.g. one table cell) together with the rest of the page, diluting away exactly the localized signal MaxSim is designed to preserve.

front: Measured Recall@3 on 8 plain factual questions: naive text RAG vs. Vision RAG?
back: Naive text RAG scored 1.000, Vision RAG scored 0.875 -- page-level retrieval is a coarser unit than a precise text chunk, so chunking wins when a document has little layout complexity.

front: What model does this page use, and what checkpoint problem does it have?
back: vidore/ColSmolVLM-256M-base -- its adapter_config.json points base_model_name_or_path at a nonexistent training-time-only local path; the fix is patching it to the real base model, HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Base.

front: How many image tokens does the example page produce, and why isn't that number fixed?
back: 1,088 tokens (17 tiles x 64 merged tokens/tile) -- it falls out of the page's pixel dimensions relative to the model's fixed 512x512 tile size, so it changes with a differently-shaped page.

front: Where does Vision RAG concretely beat naive text RAG, per the measured example?
back: On a question whose answer is a specific table cell: naive text RAG retrieves a chunk that only mentions the table and correctly declines to guess, while Vision RAG retrieves the table's page image and reads the correct value directly off it.
